title: Stalker Kills Sacramento Woman Despite Restraining Order; Mother Blames System
excerpt: Shalini Thakur, 38, was shot outside a Panera Bread in Sacramento after months of alleged stalking by 22-year-old Rohit Rohit, who later died by suicide in a police standoff.
body:
• Shalini Thakur, 38, an Indian-origin IHOP waitress, was shot dead outside a Panera Bread in Sacramento's Arden Arcade area on Tuesday after months of alleged stalking.
  • The suspect, 22-year-old Rohit Rohit, allegedly tracked her with an AirTag, slashed her tires, copied her apartment key, and violated a restraining order before fleeing police and dying by suicide.
  • The Department of Homeland Security says Rohit entered the U.S. illegally from India in 2023, was released under an order of recognizance, and was never contacted again.
  • Thakur's mother, Sudesh Kumari, says the system failed her daughter: "Restraining order after restraining order … police did not protect my daughter."

Shalini Thakur, 38, was being dropped off at work at a shopping plaza in Sacramento's Arden Arcade area on Tuesday when the man accused of stalking her for months approached and confronted her, according to the Sacramento County Sheriff's Office. When Thakur tried to flee, he chased her and shot her outside a Panera Bread restaurant near Howe and Northrop avenues. She was pronounced dead at the scene.

The suspect, identified as Rohit Rohit, 22, fled the scene but was caught up with by responding officers about two miles away. After a brief standoff, he shot himself and later died from the wound, authorities said.

Thakur's mother, Sudesh Kumari, told reporters in the aftermath that she believes the system failed to protect her daughter. "I am alone in this world," Kumari said. "Restraining order after restraining order … police did not protect my daughter."

Months of stalking before the killing

Investigators say the harassment stretched back to at least January, when Thakur found an Apple AirTag hidden under her car, according to ABC 10. What followed, authorities say, was an escalating pattern of intimidation: Rohit deflated her car tires and then followed her to work so he could pretend to offer her help. At one point, he allegedly obtained a copy of Thakur's apartment key and entered her home while she slept. When confronted, he reportedly claimed he had let himself in because he was worried something had happened to her after she failed to answer him.

He also tried to coerce her into marriage, prevented her from socializing with others, and threatened to shoot himself or anyone she met, ABC 10 reported.

Thakur knew Rohit as a DoorDash delivery driver who would park outside her home for hours and talk to her daily, investigators said. She worked as a waitress at an IHOP, where he reportedly met her while picking up delivery orders.

Thakur initially declined to pursue criminal charges or seek a restraining order, but sheriff's deputies remained in contact with her and in May urged her to obtain one, which she eventually did. On July 29, Rohit allegedly violated the order by leaving random grocery items at her front door. Deputies attempted to contact him twice after the incident, according to the sheriff's office.

Federal authorities point to immigration record

The Department of Homeland Security said Rohit, an Indian national, was taken into custody by Border Patrol agents in August 2023 while allegedly trying to enter the United States through Arizona. He was released the following month under an "order of recognizance" and DHS subsequently lost contact with him, federal officials said.

"This tragedy would have been completely avoided if it weren't for the Biden administration releasing this killer into our country."

— Department of Homeland Security spokesperson

A spokesperson for California Governor Gavin Newsom's office rejected attempts to link the killing to the state's sanctuary policies, saying the case instead raised questions about preventing stalking and domestic violence and keeping victims safe. The New York Post reported that California's sanctuary laws prohibit local law enforcement from cooperating with federal immigration enforcement — something officials said could have led to Rohit being detained or deported after he was reported to police at least twice before the killing.

Diaspora angle

Thakur's killing has landed hard in the Indian diaspora, where many immigrant women work late-shift service jobs and navigate unfamiliar legal systems alone. For families thousands of miles from home, Kumari's words have become a rallying cry — a demand that stalking complaints from vulnerable immigrant workers be taken seriously before threats become fatalities.

What's next

The Sacramento County Sheriff's Office continues its investigation, and questions remain about whether the restraining-order violations in July were followed up aggressively enough. The case has also reignited the national debate over immigration enforcement and sanctuary policies, with federal officials arguing Rohit should not have been in the country at the time of the killing. For the Indian-American community in Sacramento, attention now turns to memorial efforts and supporting Kumari, who says she has no one left.
image_caption: Sacramento County Sheriff's deputies at the scene of the shooting outside a Panera Bread in Sacramento's Arden Arcade area. Shalini Thakur, 38, was killed there after months of alleged stalking despite a restraining order.
nri_angle: An Indian-origin woman working a service job in California was killed by her alleged stalker despite a restraining order, raising urgent safety questions for immigrant workers in the diaspora.
